source.title: Picard ranks of K3 surfaces over function fields and the Hecke orbit conjecture
source.authors: Davesh Maulik, Ananth N. Shankar, Yunqing Tang
readSections: Independent reviewer Codex — codex-a71f92 read the complete 47-page author manuscript, §§1–8 and references, from https://math.berkeley.edu/~ytang/GSpincharp.pdf; creation 25 December 2021; SHA256 53f4c42762f179fba71a2d344bee56f3de1fb189f4dd9aea968a4fcbfaedc494. The original 45-page count was wrong: references occupy pp.45–47.

Published article: Inventiones mathematicae 228 (2022), 1075–1143, DOI 10.1007/s00222-022-01097-x. Public landing page/footnotes checked, full typeset text unavailable. This author manuscript is the reviewed source, NOT the version of record; source findings are scoped to it.

The prior extractor reported an arXiv-v1 source comparison (17 November 2020, archive SHA256 d1aeacc7dbdab10a09d5e9a4fd2fb6d44fc759eabcbe4d1b9fdcaed40cabf3e8). That comparison was not repeated by the reviewer; only the public version history (v1 only) was independently checked. All locators use author-manuscript numbering.

Independent review checked all 96 inherited items, six inherited routes and six inherited source findings. Clear corrections were made; reviewGaps identifies the remaining proof and decomposition work. Completed negative review does not imply completed extraction.

summary: Picard-rank jumping for generically ordinary non-isotrivial K3 families over proper curves in characteristic p≥5 with generic Picard discriminant prime to p follows via prime-to-p special-divisor intersections on hyperspecial GSpin models; the paper derives ordinary Hecke-orbit density in the stated orthogonal and split-unitary cases. This extraction is partial after independent review: upper-bound, filtration, library and normalization errors are corrected, but generalized decay, lifted valuations, compound-item decomposition and supplier comparisons remain gates. No formal proof or falsity of the main geometric theorems is claimed.

items.name: Quadratic forms, Clifford algebras and the spin group
items.statement: A quadratic form Q on a module over a commutative ring, its polarisation [x,y] = Q(x+y)-Q(x)-Q(y), the Clifford algebra C(L,Q) with its Z/2-grading and even part C^+(L), and the spin group inside C^+(L)^×.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §1.1 and §2.1, the standing data (L,Q) of signature (b,2) and its Clifford algebra
items.note: Pinned definitions read. This abstract spin group embeds into Clifford units; it is not the reductive group scheme GSpin in item17.

items.name: Lattices in a real vector space and their covolume
items.statement: A full-rank Z-lattice in a finite-dimensional real vector space, a fundamental domain for it, and its covolume.
items.locator: Author manuscript, §3 covolumes and Definition7.8, p.31 (not a numbered lattice-estimate subsection §7.2).
items.note: Mathlib has ZLattice with `ZSpan.fundamentalDomain` and `ZLattice.covolume`. The successive minima of a positive definite quadratic lattice, and the uniform lattice-point counts in terms of them, are not there; they are separate items.

items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect field and their Frobenius
items.statement: For a perfect field k of characteristic p, the ring W = W(k) of p-typical Witt vectors, its fraction field K = W[1/p], and the Frobenius automorphism σ of W and K.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.1, the standing notation k = F_p-bar, W = W(k), K = W[1/p]
items.note: Read Frobenius.lean:286, Isocrystal.lean:79 and DiscreteValuationRing.lean:143–149. FractionRing(WittVector p k) has the Frobenius automorphism; every nonzero Witt vector is a p-power times a unit, giving W[1/p]. The existing one-dimensional isocrystal classification is not general Dieudonné/Ogus theory.

items.name: Shimura data and the analytic Shimura variety at a compact open level
items.statement: For a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), construct its reflex field E, compact-open levels K⊂G(A_f), analytic quotient G(Q)\(X×G(A_f))/K and canonical model over E. Level/Hecke maps have specified source and target levels; universal families require sufficiently small prime-to-p level.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §2.1, where (G_Q, D_L) is shown to be a Shimura datum with reflex field Q and Sh(G_Q,D_L)_𝕂 is formed
items.note: D3 supplies reflex fields, D4 data/Hodge type, D5 levels, V1 the tower and V6 Hodge-type canonical models; D2 alone is not the datum definition.

items.name: Baily–Borel algebraicity and the minimal compactification in characteristic zero
items.statement: The analytic Shimura variety is a quasi-projective algebraic variety, with the Baily–Borel (minimal) compactification as a normal projective variety whose boundary is stratified by Shimura varieties of smaller dimension.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.1, where Sh^BB is the generic fibre of the integral model 𝒮^BB
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V2 plans exactly this. What the paper needs beyond it is the integral model of the minimal compactification, which is a separate missing item.

items.name: Dieudonné theory for p-divisible groups over a perfect field
items.statement: For a perfect characteristic-p field, contravariant Dieudonné theory classifies p-divisible groups by finite-free W(k)-modules with F,V, FV=VF=p, with dimensions/heights/slopes. Endomorphisms correspond to W(k)-linear ENDOMORPHISMS of this module commuting with F,V, not its invariant vectors. Restriction to the special-endomorphism subcrystal yields 𝓛=𝕃^{φ=1}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.1, where 𝓛 = 𝕃^{φ=1} is deduced from Dieudonné theory
items.note: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 plans Dieudonné theory over perfect residue fields including Frobenius, Verschiebung, slopes and the ordinary and supersingular cases. The extension over k[[t]] used in §5, de Jong's theory, is a separate missing item.

items.name: Crystals and F-crystals on a crystalline site
items.statement: On an eligible crystalline PD site, use finite locally free crystals with quasi-nilpotent integrable connections on suitable lifts, Frobenius linearizations/isogenies, isocrystals and Tate twists. The paper's weight-zero φ maps 𝕃 into p^{-1}𝕃 and need not be an integral endomorphism of 𝕃.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §2.2 and §4.8, where 𝐋_cris is an F-crystal and its horizontal sections are used
items.note: CR.1/CR.3 supply the general objects; the special tensor subobject is item19. The aggregate audit has no CR/R07 row, but A4's reviewed audit explicitly records its missing supplier interfaces; their actual stage descriptions were read.

items.name: Serre–Tate theory and Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory
items.statement: The Serre–Tate equivalence between deformations of an abelian scheme over a nilpotent thickening and deformations of its p-divisible group, the canonical coordinates on the deformation space of an ordinary abelian variety, and Grothendieck–Messing theory describing deformations by lifts of the Hodge filtration in the value of the Dieudonné crystal.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §3.5 (Serre–Tate coordinates at an ordinary point) and §5.3 (the limits of Grothendieck–Messing in equicharacteristic p)
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 plans the Serre–Tate equivalence and imports Grothendieck–Messing from FiniteFlatGroups R07.6. The paper's point is precisely that Grothendieck–Messing is too weak in equicharacteristic p, which is a separate missing item.

items.name: The Weil representation of the metaplectic group
items.statement: The metaplectic double cover and local/global Weil representation with additive characters, splittings and Haar normalizations. Its finite discriminant-module representation ρ_L on C[L^∨/L] and the vector-valued modular comparison are additional construction/comparison tasks in item67.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.2, where ρ_L is the Weil representation of Mp_2(Z) on C[L^∨/L]
items.note: MP.1/MP.4 supply the generic representation, not automatically the finite S,T matrices and normalization.

items.name: Dirichlet characters, their complex L-functions and the Riemann zeta function
items.statement: For N>0, DirichletCharacter ℂ N and its complex continuation L(χ,s), agreeing with the Dirichlet series for Re(s)>1, and riemannZeta. The discriminant character and negative/real-exponent divisor sums remain item69.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.3 and Theorem 7.4, where L(1+b/2, χ), ζ(b+1) and σ_{-b/2}(m,χ) appear in the Fourier coefficients
items.note: AUDIT-06 marks AN.1 built. The named pinned statements were read; no new L-function continuation is planned.

items.name: The modular curve and its universal elliptic curve
items.statement: Use a sufficiently small prime-to-p fine modular level, for example full N≥3 with p∤N, and its universal elliptic curve, base change and level maps. For nonfine quotients keep the stack/finite quotient and descent; no universal elliptic scheme is asserted on arbitrary coarse modular curves.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.5, where π^{-1}(Υ) is a torsor under ℰ ⊗_Z Λ over a modular curve
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur plans modular curves and their universal elliptic curves. Only the orthogonal cusp geometry built on it is specific to this paper.

items.name: Picard rank jumps in a generically ordinary family of K3 surfaces (Theorem 1.1)
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper curve over F_p-bar with p ≥ 5 and let 𝑳 → C be a generically ordinary, non-isotrivial family of K3 surfaces whose generic Picard lattice has discriminant prime to p. Then there are infinitely many c ∈ C(F_p-bar) at which the Picard rank of 𝑳_c exceeds the generic Picard rank of 𝑳.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 1.1
items.note: The first main theorem. Both hypotheses are needed: a family of supersingular K3 surfaces has constant rank 22, and the Kummer family K(E ×_C E_0) with E_0 supersingular jumps at only finitely many points.

items.name: Generically ordinary curves meet the special divisors infinitely often (Theorem 1.2)
items.statement: Let 𝒮 be the canonical integral model over Z_p of the GSpin Shimura variety of a quadratic Z-lattice (L,Q) of signature (b,2) with p ∤ disc(L,Q), b ≥ 3 and p ≥ 5. Let C be an irreducible smooth proper curve with a finite morphism C → 𝒮_{F_p-bar} whose generic point is ordinary and whose image lies in no special divisor Z(m). Then infinitely many F_p-bar-points of C lie in ∪_{m ∈ N, p ∤ m} Z(m).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 1.2, proved at the end of §7
items.note: The engine of the paper; Theorem 1.1 follows from it through the Kuga–Satake period map. For b = 2, 3 it is the earlier Maulik–Shankar–Tang paper on abelian surfaces over global function fields.

items.name: Statement of the general μ-ordinary Chai–Oort conjecture
items.statement: Conjectural target, not a theorem proved here: every μ-ordinary point on the special fibre of a hyperspecial Hodge-type Shimura variety has Zariski-dense prime-to-p Hecke orbit. Form the proposition using the open Newton stratum; the proved cases are item15 only.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Conjecture 1.3, attributed to Chai and Oort
items.note: Stated for Hodge type; Chai and Oort made it in the PEL case. The paper proves it in the orthogonal and in certain unitary cases.

items.name: The ordinary Hecke orbit conjecture for GSpin and unitary Shimura varieties (Theorem 1.4)
items.statement: Let 𝒮_{F_p} (p ≥ 5) be the mod p fibre of the canonical integral model attached to either (orthogonal case) a quadratic Z-lattice of signature (b,2) with discriminant prime to p, or (unitary case) an imaginary quadratic field K split at p and an O_K-Hermitian lattice of signature (n,1) with discriminant prime to p. Then the prime-to-p Hecke orbit of an ordinary point is dense in 𝒮_{F_p}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 1.4, proved in §8
items.note: The second main theorem, and the first result of its kind for orthogonal Shimura varieties. Its only input from the rest of the paper is the statement of Theorem 1.2.

items.name: The characteristic-zero comparison: density of Noether–Lefschetz points (Green, Oguiso)
items.statement: For a non-isotrivial family 𝑳 → Δ of compact K3 surfaces over the unit disc with minimal fibre Picard rank ρ, the set of t ∈ Δ whose fibre has Picard rank greater than ρ is a countable dense subset of Δ; in particular it is infinite.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §1.1, the result recalled from Green and Oguiso
items.note: Recalled as the statement Theorem 1.1 is the characteristic-p analogue of; it is not an input to any proof in the paper. A roadmap that plans Theorem 1.1 should carry it as the comparison statement and import variations of Hodge structure and Noether–Lefschetz loci rather than rebuild them. Historical comparison, not an input to the characteristic-p proof. Assignment to a common K3/Hodge-locus supplier remains a review gap.

items.name: The GSpin Shimura datum and its canonical integral model
items.statement: For a quadratic Z-lattice (L,Q) of signature (b,2) self-dual at p, set V = L ⊗ Q with the bilinear form [x,y] = Q(x+y)-Q(x)-Q(y) and G = GSpin(L ⊗ Z_(p), Q), a reductive group scheme over Z_(p). G(R) acts through G → SO(V) on D_L = {z ∈ V_C : [z,z]=0, [z,z-bar] < 0}/C^×; for [z] ∈ D_L the cocharacter h_{[z]}: Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R induces the Hodge decomposition V_C^{1,-1} = Cz, V_C^{0,0} = (Cz ⊕ Cz-bar)^⊥, V_C^{-1,1} = Cz-bar. Then (G_Q, D_L) is a Shimura datum with reflex field Q. For 𝕂 ⊂ G(A_f) ∩ C(L ⊗ Z-hat)^× with 𝕂_p = G(Z_p), the Shimura variety Sh = Sh(G_Q,D_L)_𝕂 over Q has, by Kisin, a canonical smooth integral model 𝒮 over Z_(p).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §2.1
items.note: This is the object every later section works with. The signature convention and the hyperspecial level at p are used throughout: self-duality at p is what makes 𝒮 smooth and the ordinary locus non-empty.

items.name: The Kuga–Satake abelian scheme and its cohomological realisations
items.statement: Let H = C(L) with its right self-action, and equip H ⊗ Z_(p) with the left G-action. A suitable symplectic form on H gives G_Q → GSp(H ⊗ Q) and a morphism of Shimura data, hence the Kuga–Satake abelian scheme A^univ → Sh with first Betti cohomology the local system 𝐇_B attached to H. It extends to an abelian scheme 𝒜^univ → 𝒮 with a left C(L)-action. Write 𝐇_dR, 𝐇_{ℓ,ét} (ℓ ≠ p) for the first relative de Rham and ℓ-adic étale cohomology of 𝒜^univ → 𝒮, and 𝐇_cris for the first relative crystalline cohomology of 𝒜^univ_{F_p} → 𝒮_{F_p}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §2.2, first paragraph
items.note: The abelian scheme is what makes special endomorphisms and hence special divisors moduli-theoretic. The relative crystalline cohomology over the special fibre is the realisation the whole characteristic-p argument runs in.

items.name: The local systems 𝐋_? inside End_{C(L)}(𝐇_?) and the quadratic form 𝐐
items.statement: Left multiplication by L on H gives a G_Q-equivariant map L ⊗ Q → End_{C(L)}(H ⊗ Q) and hence a Z-local system 𝐋_B → End_{C(L)}(𝐇_B) on Sh. There are a filtered vector bundle with connection 𝐋_dR ⊂ End_{C(L)}(𝐇_dR), a Z_ℓ-lisse sheaf 𝐋_{ℓ,ét} ⊂ End_{C(L)}(𝐇_{ℓ,ét}) and an F-crystal 𝐋_cris ⊂ End_{C(L)}(𝐇_cris), all compatible with 𝐋_B under the Betti–de Rham, Betti–étale and de Rham–crystalline comparisons. Each 𝐋_? carries a quadratic form 𝐐 defined by f ∘ f = 𝐐(f)·Id.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §2.2, second paragraph
items.note: The four realisations and their compatibility are the content of Madapusi Pera's work; the crystalline one is the only one used in the characteristic-p sections, by Remark 2.4. Notation, following the paper: bold 𝐋 and 𝐇 are the families over 𝒮 and bold 𝐐 the quadratic form on them, while blackboard 𝕃 = 𝐋_{cris,P}(W) is the fibre at a point P, as in §4.

items.name: Special endomorphisms of the Kuga–Satake scheme and of its p-divisible group
items.statement: For an 𝒮-scheme T, an endomorphism v ∈ End_{C(L)}(𝒜^univ_T) is special if all of its cohomological realisations lie in the image of 𝐋_? → End_{C(L)}(𝐇_?) for ? = B, dR, cris and (ℓ,ét) for every ℓ ≠ p, dropping the realisations that do not make sense. An endomorphism v ∈ End_{C(L)}(𝒜^univ_T[p^∞]) is special if its crystalline realisation lies in 𝐋_cris.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 2.3
items.note: Both clauses are used: the first defines the special divisors, the second the lattices 𝓛_n of formal special endomorphisms that the decay lemmas are about.

items.name: Speciality is checked at one geometric point, and crystallinely in the special fibre
items.statement: For connected T, an endomorphism of 𝒜^univ_T or of 𝒜^univ_T[p^∞] is special if and only if it is special at one geometric point t ∈ T. If moreover T_{F_p} ≠ ∅, one may take t ∈ T_{F_p}, and for such t an endomorphism is special if and only if its crystalline realisation lies in 𝐋_cris.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Remark 2.4
items.note: This is what lets the whole paper verify speciality using 𝐋_cris alone, and is quoted from Andreatta–Goren–Howard–Madapusi Pera and Madapusi Pera.

items.name: Special endomorphisms carry a positive definite quadratic form
items.statement: For a special v ∈ End_{C(L)}(𝒜^univ_T) one has v ∘ v = [Q(v)] for a unique Q(v) ∈ Z_{≥0}, and v ↦ Q(v) is a positive definite quadratic form on the Z-lattice of special endomorphisms of 𝒜^univ_T.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Remark 2.5
items.note: Positive definiteness is what turns the local intersection multiplicity into a lattice point count with bounded norm; it is quoted from Madapusi Pera.

items.name: Special divisors
items.statement: For m ∈ Z_{>0} the special divisor 𝒵(m) is the Deligne–Mumford stack over 𝒮 whose T-points, for an 𝒮-scheme T, are the special v ∈ End(𝒜^univ_T) with Q(v) = m; the same notation is used for its image in 𝒮. It is an effective Cartier divisor, flat over Z_(p), so Z(m) := 𝒵(m)_{F_p-bar} is an effective Cartier divisor of 𝒮_{F_p-bar}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 2.6
items.note: Flatness over Z_(p) is what makes the special fibre a divisor and is used again in §8 to see that Z(m) is a union of special fibres of Shimura subvarieties. Preserve the divisor stack's cycle pushforward and multiplicities, not its reduced image. Prove compatibility with the count of v and −v before comparing modular coefficients.

items.name: The tautological line bundle ω and the Hasse invariant
items.statement: ω is the tautological line bundle on 𝒮_{F_p-bar} attached to Fil^1 V ⊂ V, that is the line bundle of weight-one modular forms; the Hasse invariant H is a section of ω^{p-1} whose vanishing locus is the non-ordinary locus, and for P ∈ C(k) one sets h_P = v_t(H|_{C-hat_P}).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 7.6 and Lemma 7.5
items.note: That H is a section of ω^{p-1} is what gives Σ_P h_P = (p-1)(ω.C), the identity that balances the local and global counts.

items.name: Local intersection multiplicities are lattice point counts
items.statement: Let P ∈ (C ∩ Z(m))(k), let t be a local coordinate at P so that C-hat_P = Spf k[[t]], let 𝒜/k[[t]] be the pullback of 𝒜^univ and let L_n be the Z-lattice of special endomorphisms of 𝒜 mod t^n. If C is contained in no special divisor then i_P(C.Z(m)) = Σ_{n≥1} #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, equation (3.1), repeated as (7.1) in §7.7
items.note: The bridge between intersection theory and lattices. It needs the moduli description of 𝒵(m) and proper intersection, which is where the hypothesis that C lies in no Z(m) is used.

items.name: The nested lattices L_n and the supersingular rank dichotomy
items.statement: The L_n form a decreasing chain with ∩_n L_n = 0, all of the same rank, and L_1/L_n is a p-group; 𝓛_n := L_n ⊗ Z_p is the lattice of special endomorphisms of 𝒜[p^∞] mod t^n. Moreover rk_Z L_1 = b+2 if and only if P is supersingular, and rk_Z L_1 ≤ b otherwise, because the Frobenius on 𝐋_{cris,P}(W) has weight 0 and so its non-zero-slope part cannot have rank b+1.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.7, with the rank statement from Howard–Pappas Lemma 4.2.4
items.note: The dichotomy is why supersingular points are the whole difficulty: they are exactly the points where the lattice of special endomorphisms has full rank b+2 and the local count has the same order of magnitude as the global one.

items.name: Cusps of the GSpin Baily–Borel compactification
items.statement: For a GSpin Shimura variety the boundary components of 𝒮^BB are either 0-dimensional or 1-dimensional; a 1-dimensional cusp Υ corresponds to a saturated isotropic sublattice I ⊂ L of rank 2, with Λ = I^⊥/I.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.1, following Bruinier–Zemel §§3.2–3.3 and Zemel §4
items.note: The dichotomy of cusp dimensions is what makes the case analysis of §8 finite; the explicit isotropic sublattice is what identifies the fibres of π in the next item.

items.name: The fibres over a 1-dimensional cusp are abelian-scheme torsors over a modular curve
items.statement: Up to a quotient by a finite group, π^{-1}(Υ) is a torsor under the abelian scheme ℰ ⊗_Z Λ over the modular curve Υ, where ℰ is the universal elliptic curve and Λ = I^⊥/I for the isotropic rank-2 sublattice I attached to Υ; the same description holds integrally by Madapusi Pera's Theorem 4.1.5.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.5, from Zemel Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5 and Bruinier–Zemel Lemma 3.18 and Proposition 3.19
items.note: This is the geometric input to Proposition 8.6: the Hecke translates by the unipotent radical are translations by torsion points of ℰ_{π(y)} ⊗ Λ.

items.name: The decay thresholds h_r and h'_r
items.statement: For a point P with h_P = v_t(H) and a = h_P/2, set h_r = [h_P(p^r + ··· + p + 1 + 1/p)] for r ≥ 0, h'_r = [h_P(p^r + ··· + 1) + a/p] and h'_{-1} = [a/p].
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 3.1
items.note: Two families of thresholds: the unprimed ones govern non-superspecial supersingular points, the primed ones superspecial points, where the extra a/p records the faster decay.

items.name: Decay of the index at a non-superspecial supersingular point (Theorem 3.2)
items.statement: Let P be supersingular but not superspecial. Then |L_1/L_n| ≥ p^{2+2r} whenever h_r + 1 ≤ n ≤ h_{r+1}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 3.2, deduced from Theorem 5.2
items.note: In words: past h_P(1+1/p) the abelian scheme mod t^n has strictly fewer special endomorphisms than mod t, with index at least p^2, and the index doubles in exponent at each further threshold.

items.name: Decay of the index at a superspecial point (Theorem 3.3)
items.statement: Let P be superspecial. Then one of the following holds. (1) |L_1/L_n| ≥ p^{1+2r} if h'_{r-1} + ap^r + 1 ≤ n ≤ h'_r, and |L_1/L_n| ≥ p^{2+2r} if h'_r + 1 ≤ n ≤ h'_r + ap^{r+1}. (2) |L_1/L_n| ≥ p if h'_{-1} + a + 1 ≤ n ≤ h'_0, and |L_1/L_n| ≥ p^{3+2r} if h'_r + 1 ≤ n ≤ h'_{r+1}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 3.3, deduced from Theorem 6.2
items.note: Superspecial points need the stronger statement because their lattice of special endomorphisms is as large as possible; the dichotomy mirrors the two cases of Theorem 6.2. The singularity of the non-ordinary locus at superspecial points is what forces the faster decay.

items.name: The heuristic count of branches and the balance with the global intersection
items.statement: Heuristic only: assuming EVERY nonordinary point of C is superspecial, Σ_{P superspecial}h_P=(p−1)(ω.C), and the approximate branch count |q_L(m)|/p^{t_P/2} motivates the stronger decay. Without that assumption the superspecial sum is only ≤ the Hasse degree. This is not an individual-m asymptotic theorem.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §3.4
items.note: This paragraph explains why superspecial points need a strictly stronger decay statement than supersingular ones, and why the theorem is false without the generic-ordinariness hypothesis.

items.name: A formal curve whose local multiplicities grow exponentially
items.statement: At an ordinary point with Serre–Tate coordinates {q_i,q'_i}, choose μ ∈ Z_p^× very well approximated by integers and define Spf k[[t]] ⊂ 𝒮_k by q_i ↦ (1+α_i t)^{-μ}, q'_i ↦ 1 + α_i t with α_i ∈ k linearly independent over F_p. Then 𝒜/Spf k[[t]] has no non-zero special endomorphism while 𝒜[p^∞] has special endomorphisms spanned by the e_i + μ f_i, and for a suitable sequence m_j ≍ p^{2n_j} one has i_P(Spf k[[t]] . Z(m_j)) ≥ p^{n_{j+1}}, which is exponential in m_j.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §3.5
items.note: The point of the example: no purely local argument can bound the local multiplicities, so the proof must use that C is algebraic, through the global bound i_P(C.Z(m)) ≤ C.Z(m). It also uses that the locus where Σ(λ_i e_i + μ_i f_i) deforms is cut out by ∏ q_i^{λ_i} q'^{μ_i} - 1.

items.name: The crystal at a supersingular point and its Frobenius-invariants
items.statement: For a supersingular point P set 𝕃 = 𝐋_{cris,P}(W), a W-quadratic space for 𝐐 with a σ-linear Frobenius φ that is not an endomorphism of 𝕃 but a map 𝕃 → (1/p)𝕃 satisfying ⟨φx,φy⟩ = σ⟨x,y⟩. Let 𝓛 be the Z_p-lattice of special endomorphisms of A_P[p^∞]; then 𝓛 = 𝕃^{φ=1}, and rk_{Z_p} 𝓛 = rk_W 𝕃 = rk_Z L with 𝕃 ⊂ 𝓛 ⊗ K.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.1
items.note: Supersingularity is exactly the statement that φ is isoclinic of slope 0 on 𝕃, so that the Frobenius-invariants have full rank; this is what makes Ogus's classification apply.

items.name: Ogus's orthogonal decomposition and the type of a supersingular point
items.statement: There is a decomposition of Z_p-quadratic lattices (𝓛,⟨,⟩) = (𝓛_0,⟨,⟩_0) ⊕ (𝓛_1,⟨,⟩_1) with p | ⟨,⟩_0, with both (1/p)⟨,⟩_0 and ⟨,⟩_1 perfect, and with rk_{Z_p} 𝓛_0 even; p⟨,⟩_0 induces a perfect F_p-valued quadratic form on (1/p)𝓛_0/𝓛_0. The type t_P := rk_{Z_p} 𝓛_0 is even and satisfies 2 ≤ t_P ≤ rk L. P is superspecial if t_P = 2 and non-superspecial otherwise.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.1, from Ogus, Supersingular K3 crystals, Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.11
items.note: t_P/2 is the Artin invariant when A_P is the Kuga–Satake abelian variety of a K3 surface. The decomposition is the starting point of the whole explicit computation of §§4–6.

items.name: The induced decomposition of the crystal
items.statement: The decomposition of 𝓛 induces 𝕃 = 𝕃_0 ⊕ 𝕃_1 with 𝓛_0 ⊗ W ⊂ 𝕃_0 ⊂ (1/p)𝓛_0 ⊗ W, with 𝕃_0 mod 𝓛_0 ⊗ W a totally isotropic subspace of ((1/p)𝓛_0/𝓛_0) ⊗ k of dimension t_P/2 subject to Ogus's conditions, and 𝕃_1 = 𝓛_1 ⊗ W.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.2, from Ogus, Supersingular K3 crystals, Theorems 3.5 and 3.20
items.note: The moduli of supersingular crystals sits entirely in 𝕃_0; 𝕃_1 is determined by 𝓛_1 and carries φ = 1 ⊗ σ.

items.name: A normal form for 𝓛_0 (Lemma 4.3)
items.statement: Let n=t_P/2. Choose u∈Z_p^× nonsquare mod p and λ∈Z_{p²}^× with λ²=u and σ(λ)=−λ (a suitable Teichmüller choice). There is a Z_p-basis e_i,f_i of 𝓛_0 with ⟨e_i,f_i⟩=p for i>1, ⟨e_1,e_1⟩=2p, ⟨f_1,f_1⟩=−2up, symmetric partners understood and all other entries zero. The mere condition on λ² mod p does not ensure a Z_p-valued matrix.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 4.3, attributed to Ogus
items.note: 𝓛_0 depends only on t_P; 𝓛_1 depends on dim L and disc L. The non-residue λ is what makes the first hyperbolic-like block anisotropic.

items.name: Classification of the crystals 𝕃_0 over a fixed 𝓛_0 (Lemma 4.4)
items.statement: With 𝓛_0 as in Lemma 4.3, all 𝕃 attached to a supersingular point with (𝕃_0)^{φ=1} = 𝓛_0 are 𝕃_0 = Span_W{v,σv,…,σ^{n-1}v} + 𝓛_0 ⊗ W for a v ∈ (1/p)(𝓛_0 ⊗ W) with: (1) Span_W{v,…,σ^{2n-1}v} = (1/p)𝓛_0 ⊗ W; (2) Span_W{v,…,σ^{n-1}v} isotropic for ⟨,⟩_0; (3) ⟨v,σ^n v⟩_0 = 1/p. The quadratic form and φ = 1 ⊗ σ are induced from 𝓛_0 ⊗ K, and {v,…,σ^{n-1}v, pσ^n v,…,pσ^{2n-1}v} is a W-basis of 𝕃_0.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 4.4, attributed to Ogus
items.note: Proved from Ogus's Theorem 3.5 together with the paragraph before his Theorem 3.21, Hensel's lemma and a unit rescaling. The cyclic vector v is the whole content of the classification.

items.name: A cyclic Frobenius normal form (Lemma 4.5)
items.statement: In the W-basis v_1,…,v_n,w_1,…,w_n, the Gram matrix is [[0,I],[I,0]]. The σ-linear Frobenius satisfies φ(v_i)=v_{i+1} for i<n, φ(v_n)=p^{-1}w_1, φ(w_i)=w_{i+1}−b_iw_1 for i<n, φ(w_n)=pv_1+pΣ_{i=1}^{n−1}b_iv_{i+1}, with b_i∈W.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 4.5
items.note: The explicit B_0 is what all the matrix computations of §§5–6 are built on. Its proof is essentially Ogus's Lemma 3.22, run in the paper's weight-0 normalisation.

items.name: The change-of-basis matrices S_0 and S'_0
items.statement: S_0 ∈ M_{2n}(K) has as its first n (resp. last n) columns the coordinates of v_i (resp. w_i) in the basis {e_i,f_i}; S'_0 is the corresponding matrix for {pv_i,w_i}. Then S'_0 ∈ GL_{2n}(W) and S_0 = S'_0 · diag(p^{-1}I, I).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.6
items.note: Only S'_0 is integral; keeping track of which of the two is used is what controls the p-adic valuations in §5.

items.name: The three cases for 𝓛_1 and the reduction to the split case
items.statement: 𝓛_1 is self-dual, so either (1) dim 𝓛_1 = 2m with an m-dimensional isotropic Z_p-subspace (the split case), or (2) dim 𝓛_1 = 2m with no such subspace, or (3) dim 𝓛_1 is odd. In cases (2) and (3) one embeds 𝓛_1 into a split Z_p-quadratic lattice of larger dimension, so it suffices to treat the split case, where {e'_i,f'_i}_{i=1}^m is a basis with the standard hyperbolic Gram matrix.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.7
items.note: The embedding trick is used again inside the proofs of Theorems 5.2 and 6.2; the accepted version spells out that the enlarged lattice is chosen even-dimensional, of signature (b',2), self-dual at p and non-split mod p.

items.name: Kisin's description of the deformation space and the F-crystal on it
items.statement: In the split setup n=t_P/2, rank𝓛_1=2m, the completed local ring is R=W[[x_i,y_i,x'_j,y'_j]] (1≤i<n,1≤j≤m), with the opposite-unipotent tautological point u and Frob=u(φ⊗σ); σ raises formal coordinates to their pth powers. The filtration is Fil¹=k·w̄_n, Fil⁰=span{v̄_i:i<n;w̄_j:j≤n;ē'_l,f̄'_l:l≤m}, Fil⁻¹=𝕃⊗k. Fil⁰ includes w̄_n and excludes v̄_n. Transcribing every entry of u and its API remains a decomposition obligation.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.8, following Kisin §§1.4–1.5
items.note: This is the object the decay lemmas analyse: the whole local structure of the Shimura variety at a supersingular point, together with the crystal of special endomorphisms over it, in coordinates.

items.name: The equation of the non-ordinary locus in the crystal (Lemma 4.9)
items.statement: For a supersingular point P the non-ordinary locus over k in the formal neighbourhood of P is cut out by the vanishing of the map p·Frob induced on gr^{-1} 𝐋_cris(R ⊗_W k).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 4.9, attributed to Ogus
items.note: The Hodge filtration on 𝐋_cris(R ⊗ k) is the constant extension of the one at P, and p·Frob preserves it; ordinarity is the non-vanishing of the induced map on the bottom graded piece.

items.name: The explicit equation of the non-ordinary locus (Corollary 4.10)
items.statement: For a supersingular point P the non-ordinary locus over k in the formal neighbourhood of P is cut out by Q = 0 if P is superspecial, and by y_1 = 0 otherwise.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Corollary 4.10
items.note: This is the source of the dichotomy in Theorems 3.2 and 3.3: at a superspecial point the non-ordinary locus is a quadric cone, singular at P, while elsewhere it is smooth.

items.name: Frobenius in the φ-invariant basis
items.statement: Viewing {e_i,f_i,e'_j,f'_j} as an R[1/p]-basis of 𝐋_cris(R) ⊗ R[1/p], one has Frob = S(uB)σ(S^{-1})∘σ = S'u'(S')^{-1}∘σ, where S = diag(S_0,I), S' = diag(S'_0,I) ∈ GL_{2n+2m}(W) and u' is the explicit unipotent matrix obtained from u by dividing its (n, ·) row entries and the first n entries of the last column by p.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §4.11
items.note: Working in the φ-invariant basis is what lets the horizontal section of a special endomorphism be written as an explicit infinite matrix product in §5.

items.name: Rapid decay of a special endomorphism
items.statement: With h the t-adic valuation of the local equation of the non-ordinary locus and h_r = [h(p^r + ··· + 1 + 1/p)], a vector w ∈ 𝓛 decays rapidly if for every r ≥ 0 the special endomorphism p^r w does not lift to an endomorphism of 𝒜[p^∞] modulo t^{h_r+1}; a Z_p-submodule decays rapidly if every primitive vector in it does.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 5.1, from Maulik–Shankar–Tang, Reductions of abelian surfaces over global function fields, Definition 5.1.1
items.note: The definition is about lifting to the p-divisible group, not to the abelian scheme; that is what makes it checkable inside the crystal.

items.name: The Decay Lemma in the generic case (Theorem 5.2)
items.statement: For a generically ordinary formal curve specialising to a non-superspecial supersingular point there is a saturated Z_p-submodule of 𝓛 of rank 2 that decays rapidly.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 5.2
items.note: Theorem 3.2 follows at once: choosing a basis of 𝓛 extending one of the rapidly decaying submodule gives |𝓛/𝓛_n| ≥ p^{2r+2} for n ≥ h_r+1, and 𝓛_n = L_n ⊗ Z_p. The proof actually produces a submodule of rank at least n = t_P/2.

items.name: Why Grothendieck–Messing theory is not enough in equicharacteristic p
items.statement: Over Spec k[t]/(t^a) → Spec k[t]/(t^{pa}) the natural divided powers make the Dieudonné crystal evaluate on the larger ring, so any endomorphism α of a p-divisible group over k[t]/(t^a) has pα deforming over k[t]/(t^{pa}), whatever α does. Hence Grothendieck–Messing gives no effective b with pα not extending mod t^b, unlike the mixed-characteristic case where α lifting mod p^n but not p^{n+1} forces pα to lift mod p^{n+1} but not p^{n+2}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §5.3
items.note: This is the precise obstruction that forces the explicit crystalline computation of §§4–6; it is the structural reason the characteristic-p argument is harder than the number-field one.

items.name: Horizontal sections and the infinite Frobenius product
items.statement: Over the universal ring R, form F'=S'(u'−I)(S')^{-1} and ∏_{a≥0}(I+σ^a(F')) in the formal-coordinate topology after inverting p. Applied to w∈𝓛 this is its horizontal Frobenius-stable continuation, equivalently lim Frob^a(w). FIRST twist in R, THEN substitute coefficientwise Teichmüller lifts of the curve coordinates. This need not equal twisting an arbitrary lift after substitution. The resulting F_∞ lies in M_{2n+2m}(K[[t]]) t-adically; p-adic denominators may be unbounded, not valuations tending to +∞. No universal −∞ assertion is made for zero or constant sections.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §§5.4 and 5.6, following Kisin §1.5.5
items.note: The whole of §§5–6 is the study of which coefficients of F_∞ w fail to be p-integral, and at which t-adic order.

items.name: Coordinates of the formal curve and the valuations a_i
items.statement: The formal curve gives W[[x_i,y_i,x'_j,y'_j]] → k[[t]]; let X_i(t), Y_i(t), X'_j(t), Y'_j(t) ∈ W[[t]] have as coefficients the Teichmüller lifts of those of the images. Set Y_n(t) = -Σ_{i<n} X_i Y_i - Σ_j X'_j Y'_j and Y_{n+1}(t) = -Σ_j (X'_j (Y'_j)^p + (X'_j)^p Y'_j), and a_i = v_t(Y_i(t)) for 1 ≤ i ≤ n+1. For a non-superspecial supersingular point the non-ordinary locus is y_1 = 0, so h = a_1.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §5.5
items.note: Y_n is the coordinate Q of §4.8 and Y_{n+1} comes from the block C·D^{(1)}; both are needed because the shift matrix of B_0 has length n+1.

items.name: de Jong's criterion for lifting over a truncated base
items.statement: For s≥1 use D_s of item97. If w lifts to a special endomorphism of the p-divisible group modulo t^s, its unique rational horizontal continuation lies in the integral special crystal evaluated on D_s. Thus failure of integrality obstructs lifting. Only this necessary condition is used; sufficiency or an exact maximum lift depth needs a separate theorem. Its consumer-specific calculation must prove t^N/p∉D_s for N<ps in the appropriate torsion-free presentation; the completion and coefficientwise integrality hypotheses must be stated.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §5.6
items.note: This turns a deformation-theoretic question into an explicit question about valuations of power-series coefficients, and is the step that replaces Grothendieck–Messing.

items.name: The matrices K_i and the decomposition of F_∞
items.statement: In u'−I after substitution, take blocks A,C,D of dimensions 2n×2n, 2n×2m, 2m×2n. For i<n, A_i(n,n+i)=Y_i/p and A_i(i,2n)=−Y_i/p; A_n has only A_n(n,2n)=Y_n/p. Let K_i=S'_0A_i(S'_0)^{-1}; A_{n+1}=CD^{(1)}, K_{n+1}=S'_0A_{n+1}((S'_0)^{-1})^{(1)}. The integral remainder B=B_1+B_2 has conjugated entries B_1(n,j)=X_j and B_2(n+j,2n)=−X_j for 1≤j<n, all others zero.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §5.7
items.note: The K_i are the building blocks of the top-left block F_∞(1), which is all that is needed for the Decay Lemma; R_1,…,R_{2n} denote the rows of (S'_0)^{-1}.

items.name: The Frobenius action on the rows of (S'_0)^{-1} (Lemma 5.8)
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 5.8
items.note: A direct translation of the matrix B_0 of Lemma 4.5 into the dual basis; it is what makes the products of the K_i computable.

items.name: Products of the K_i have rank one with an explicit row (Lemma 5.9)
items.statement: For 1≤i,j,l≤n+1 with l<i, K_iK_j^{(l)}=0. For l=i it equals S'_0M, with only row n possibly nonzero, namely Y_iY_j^{(i)}p^{-2}σ^{i+j−1}(R_{n+1}). For a tuple of length d≥2, ∏_{j=1}^d K_{i_j}^{(i_1+…+i_{j−1})}=S'_0M, whose row n is p^{-d}(∏_{j=1}^dY_{i_j}^{(i_1+…+i_{j−1})})σ^{i_1+…+i_d−1}(R_{n+1}); other rows vanish. The image is contained in K[[t]]·v_n; after passing to K((t)), rank is one if the scalar is nonzero. A length-one K_i for i<n generally has rank two; zero factors give zero.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 5.9
items.note: This rank-one structure is what reduces the whole computation to a single row, and hence to a linear-algebra statement over F_p in Lemmas 5.12 and 5.13.

items.name: Minimal index tuples and their weights
items.statement: For tuples I=(i_1,…,i_r)∈{1,…,n+1}^r define μ_I=Σi_j and ν_I=Σ_{j=1}^r p^{i_1+…+i_{j−1}}a_{i_j}, allowing ∞ for zero Y. Let ν_r=min_Iν_I and I_r^min={I:ν_I=ν_r}. Identifying these combinatorial minimizers with nonzero coefficient terms of exact p-adic valuation −r is a separate claim, subject to E14.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §5.10
items.note: The combinatorics of 𝑰^min_r is the heart of the proof of Theorem 5.2; ν_r is compared with the thresholds h_r at the very end.

items.name: Structure of the minimal tuples (Lemma 5.11)
items.statement: For I = (i_1,…,i_r) ∈ 𝑰^min_r: (1) (i_2,…,i_r) ∈ 𝑰^min_{r-1}, and conversely every element of 𝑰^min_{r-1} extends; (2) i_1 ≤ ··· ≤ i_r and a_{i_1} ≥ ··· ≥ a_{i_r}; (3) 𝑰^min_r is closed under coordinatewise choice between two of its elements; (4) any two elements have weights differing by less than n+1; (5) if |𝑰^min_r| > 1 then two elements have different weights, and there are a unique element of maximal and a unique element of minimal weight.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 5.11
items.note: Clauses (4) and (5) are the ones used: they bound the number of σ-twists of R-bar_{n+1} that occur, and guarantee that the extreme coefficients are non-zero. The inherited extraction silently used the intended coordinatewise-closure formulation rather than the source's reversed clause(3); this correction is now registered. Identifying ν_I with actual leading p-adic orders remains subject to the lift-valuation gap.

items.name: The row R-bar_{n+1} is F_p-anisotropic (Lemma 5.12)
items.statement: For every non-zero v ∈ F_p^{2n} one has R-bar_{n+1} v ≠ 0; consequently, for a basis {z_1,…,z_{2n}} of F_p^{2n} the elements R-bar_{n+1} z_1,…,R-bar_{n+1} z_{2n} ∈ k are linearly independent over F_p.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 5.12
items.note: This is where Lemma 4.3's anisotropic block enters; it is the arithmetic input that makes the kernels in Lemma 5.13 small.

items.name: Kernels of linear combinations of twists of R-bar_{n+1} (Lemma 5.13)
items.statement: For α_0,…,α_n ∈ k not all zero and R-bar = Σ_{i=0}^n α_i σ^i(R-bar_{n+1}), one has dim_{F_p}{v ∈ F_p^{2n} : R-bar v = 0} ≤ n.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 5.13
items.note: Together with Lemma 5.11 this gives a saturated submodule of 𝓛 of rank at least n on which no primitive vector lies in any of the kernels, which is exactly rapid decay.

items.name: The reduction step and the Claim in the proof of Theorem 5.2
items.statement: Define M_{r+1} by Σ_{I∈I^min_{r+1}}P_I=t^{ν_{r+1}}S'_0M_{r+1}+t^{ν_{r+1}+1}N_{r+1}. Because S'_0∈GL_{2n}(W), multiplication by it preserves the relevant mod-p kernels. The intended argument constructs increasing subspaces S_j=ker(p^jM_j mod p)∩F_p^{2n}, each of dimension≤n; their union is a subspace of dimension≤n. A complementary subspace lifts to a saturated rank≥n Z_p-module avoiding every kernel. For ordinary generic point ν_{r+2}≤hΣ_{j=0}^{r+1}p^j implies ν_{r+2}/p<h_r+1. Applying this to the actual coefficients requires the lift-valuation gate to be discharged.
items.locator: Author manuscript, proof of Theorem5.2 pp.24–25, before numbered paragraph5.14
items.note: The increasing-kernel argument, not arbitrary simultaneous avoidance, is required. The s>1 replacement in §5.14 is separately gated by E13.

items.name: The Decay Lemma in a general Newton stratum (Theorem 5.15)
items.statement: For a formal curve with supersingular closed point of type2n and generic open Newton codimension s−1≤n−1, §5.14 proposes saturated rank-n rapid decay. But ν_(s,…,s)=a_sΣ_{j=0}^{r+1}p^{sj} for length r+2, not a_sΣp^j. The p-based Definition5.1 bound with h=a_s is therefore NOT established for s>1 by this proof. Retain the generalized-decay target as a source-proof gap: a p^s-spaced threshold with the PD cutoff checked, or another proof, is required. The exponent objection disappears for s=1.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 5.15
items.note: Not an unconditional supplier or an approved final theorem of the design. The ordinary main theorems do not use this generalization.

items.name: Rapid and very rapid decay at a superspecial point
items.statement: For a superspecial point P and some a ≤ h/2 independent of r, with h'_r = [h(p^r+···+1) + a/p] and h'_{-1} = [a/p]: w ∈ 𝓛 decays rapidly (resp. very rapidly) if for every r ≥ 0 the endomorphism p^r w does not lift modulo t^{h'_r+1} (resp. t^{h'_{r-1}+ap^r+1}); w decays rapidly (resp. very rapidly) to first order if w does not extend modulo t^{[h+a/p]+1} (resp. t^{[a+a/p]+1}); a submodule decays rapidly if every primitive vector does; and for a rapidly decaying Λ ⊂ 𝓛 and w ∈ 𝓛 \ Λ, the pair (Λ,w) decays very rapidly to first order if w does and every primitive vector of Span_{Z_p}{Λ,w} decays rapidly to first order.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 6.1, with the corrected symbol Λ (see sourceIssues)
items.note: This definition is strictly stronger than Definition 5.1: the thresholds h'_r are smaller than h_r by roughly a, which is what buys the factor of two in the final estimate.

items.name: The Decay Lemma in the superspecial case (Theorem 6.2)
items.statement: For a generically ordinary formal curve specialising to a superspecial point there is a saturated rank-2 Z_p-submodule Λ ⊂ 𝓛 that decays rapidly, and moreover at least one of: (1) some primitive w ∈ Λ decays very rapidly; (2) some primitive w ∈ 𝓛 with w ∉ Λ is such that the pair (Λ,w) decays very rapidly to first order.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 6.2, with the corrected symbol Λ (see sourceIssues)
items.note: The two alternatives are exactly the two cases of Theorem 3.3, and they are what makes the superspecial contribution at most about half of the global intersection number instead of all of it. The authors expect the stronger rank-3 statement of their earlier paper to hold here too.

items.name: The superspecial setup and the Frobenius matrix
items.statement: At a superspecial point n = t_P/2 = 1, so 𝓛_0 has rank 2 with ⟨e_1,e_1⟩_0 = 2p and ⟨f_1,f_1⟩_0 = -2λ^2 p, the non-ordinary locus is Q = 0, and the coordinates of §4.8 reduce accordingly; the computation is carried out in the split case of §4.7 and the general case follows by the embedding trick.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §§6.3 and 6.4
items.note: The singularity of the non-ordinary locus at a superspecial point, a quadric cone rather than a smooth divisor, is what produces the extra parameter a in Definition 6.1. Define h from Q mod p, not the t-valuation of the characteristic-zero lifted sum; see the Teichmüller-cancellation finding.

items.name: The minimal-valuation terms in the superspecial expansion (Lemma 6.5)
items.statement: Fix r ≥ 0. (1) Among the terms of the product expansion of F_∞(1,3) of p-adic valuation -(r+1), those of smallest t-adic valuation lie in the set 𝑺_{1,r+1} of products F_{l,m+1}∏_{i≤α}F_t^{(i)}∏_{j≤β}F_r^{(α+2j-1)}F_l^{(α+2j)} with α+β = r+1. (2) Among those of F_∞(2,3)_s of p-adic valuation -(r+1), the minimal ones lie in the analogous set 𝑺_{2,s,r+1} with an extra factor F_{r,s}^{(α+2β+1)} and α+β = r.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 6.5
items.note: The superspecial analogue of Lemma 5.9: it identifies the finitely many products that can contribute at each p-adic level. The p-denominator count must be justified after cancellation/reduction; a sum of Teichmüller products can have nonunit leading coefficient.

items.name: Evaluation of the minimal products (Lemma 6.6)
items.statement: For α,β≥0 and α+β>0 let P_{α,β}=(∏_{i=1}^αF_t^{(i)})(∏_{j=1}^βF_r^{(α+2j−1)}F_l^{(α+2j)}), with σ(λ)=−λ. Put c=p^{−(α+β)}(∏_iQ^{(i)})(∏_jR^{(α+2j−1)}). Then P=cM^{(1)} for odd α and cN^{(1)} for even α. For α=β=0, P=I instead. The mod-p kernel exclusions require a nonzero reduced scalar after clearing p-denominators; zero reduced factors can give the full kernel. Use P_{α,β}, not P_{α+β}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 6.6
items.note: The two excluded classes of kernel vectors are exactly what produce the two alternatives of Theorem 6.2.

items.name: A positive-density set of represented integers prime to p
items.statement: Fix S ⊂ Z_{>0} of positive density with every m ∈ S represented by (L,Q) and prime to p, which exists because L may be taken maximal, so every large m is represented; for X ∈ Z_{>0} set S_X = {m ∈ S : X ≤ m ≤ 2X}. One may also assume that L is maximal and that C lies in no special divisor.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.1
items.note: Averaging over S_X rather than over all m is what makes the error terms in Propositions 7.13 and 7.17 acceptable; p ∤ m is what keeps the special divisors at hyperspecial level in §8.

items.name: The vector-valued Eisenstein series E_0 of weight 1+b/2
items.statement: With L^∨ the dual lattice, {𝔢_μ}_{μ ∈ L^∨/L} the standard basis of C[L^∨/L] and ρ_L the Weil representation of Mp_2(Z) on it, set E_0(τ) = Σ_{(g,σ) ∈ Γ'_∞\Mp_2(Z)} σ(τ)^{-(2+b)}ρ_L(g,σ)^{-1}𝔢_0. Its constant term is 𝔢_0 and it is a modular form of weight 1 + b/2 for ρ_L.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.2
items.note: E_0 is the Eisenstein part of the Borcherds generating series, and its Fourier coefficients q_L(m) are the main term of the global intersection numbers. Constant term e_0 here, versus 2e_0 in the pending SSTT bridge. Require an explicit factor-two and divisor-multiplicity comparison before identifying coefficients.

items.name: Local representation densities of a quadratic lattice
items.statement: For a quadratic Z-lattice (L,Q), det(L) is the determinant of its Gram matrix, and for a rational prime ℓ the local density is δ(ℓ,L,m) = lim_{a→∞} ℓ^{a(1-rk L)}#{v ∈ L/ℓ^a L : Q(v) ≡ m mod ℓ^a}. If m is represented by (L ⊗ Z_ℓ, Q) then δ(ℓ,L,m) > 0; moreover for rk L ≥ 5 and a fixed ℓ one has δ(ℓ,L,m) ≍ 1 for every m represented over Z_ℓ.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.3
items.note: The uniform bound δ(ℓ,L,m) ≍ 1 for rk L ≥ 5 is the reason the hypothesis b ≥ 3 appears in Theorem 1.2; it is quoted from Iwaniec. The bound δ(p,L'_n,m) ≤ 2, and ≤ 1+p^{-1} in the superspecial case, is proved in Lemma 7.16 and is separate. GN.3 explicitly plans local densities; AUDIT-02 says absent from the libraries, not the atlas.

items.name: Kronecker-symbol Dirichlet characters and twisted divisor sums
items.statement: For a non-zero D ∈ Z with D ≡ 0,1 mod 4, χ_D(a) = (D/a) is the Dirichlet character given by the Kronecker symbol; for a Dirichlet character χ one sets σ_s(m,χ) = Σ_{d|m}χ(d)d^s.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.3
items.note: These are the characters appearing in the Fourier coefficients of Theorems 7.4 and 7.15; the discriminants D are built from det L and, in the odd case, from the square-free part of m. Reuse TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantCharFun (including −4,±8) and DirichletCharacter.twistedDivisorSum for natural exponents, both read at the pin. Missing here are the arbitrary D≠0,D≡0,1 mod4 bundled comparison including imprimitive factors, and negative/real exponents such as −b/2.

items.name: The Bruinier–Kuss formula for the Fourier coefficients of E_0 (Theorem 7.4)
items.statement: For the fixed maximal integral lattice L of signature(b,2), b≥3, put Δ=det L, d=|L^∨/L| and C_b(m)=2^{1+b/2}π^{1+b/2}m^{b/2}/Γ(1+b/2), m>0. If b even, χ=χ_{(−1)^{1+b/2}4Δ} gives q_L(m)=−C_b(m)σ_{−b/2}(m,χ)/(√d L(1+b/2,χ))·∏_{ℓ|2Δ}δ(ℓ,L,m). If b odd, write m=m_0f², (f,2Δ)=1, v_ℓ(m_0)∈{0,1} for ℓ∤2Δ, D=(−1)^{(b−1)/2}2m_0Δ. Then q_L(m)=−C_b(m)L((b+1)/2,χ_D)/(√d ζ(b+1))·[Σ_{a|f}μ(a)χ_D(a)a^{−(b+1)/2}σ_{−b}(f/a)]·∏_{ℓ|2Δ}[δ(ℓ,L,m)/(1−ℓ^{−1−b})]. Here σ without a character is untwisted. For represented m>0, |q_L(m)|≍m^{b/2}, with fixed-L constants.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 7.4, quoted from Bruinier–Kuss Theorem 11 in the normalisation of Bruinier's Theorems 2.3 and 2.4
items.note: Only the last clause, |q_L(m)| ≍ m^{b/2}, is used directly, but it is deduced from the explicit formulae together with δ(ℓ,L,m) ≍ 1.

items.name: Modularity of the generating series and the global intersection asymptotic (Lemma 7.5)
items.statement: By Borcherds's modularity theorem, in its arithmetic form due to Howard and Madapusi Pera, -(ω.C) + Σ_{m≥1}(Z(m).C)q^m is the 𝔢_0-component of a vector-valued modular form of weight 1+b/2 for ρ_L whose Eisenstein part is the 𝔢_0-component of -(ω.C)E_0. Hence Z(m).C = |q_L(m)|(ω.C) + O(m^{(b+2)/4}), and Σ_{m ∈ S_X} Z(m).C ≍ (ω.C)Σ_{m ∈ S_X}|q_L(m)| ≍ X^{1+b/2}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 7.5
items.note: The error term is the trivial bound on the Fourier coefficients of a cusp form of weight 1+b/2. This is the only global input, and it is what the local bounds must be compared against.

items.name: The expected local share g_P(m) of the global intersection number
items.statement: For every P∈C(k), set g_P(m)=h_P|q_L(m)|/(p−1), where h_P is the pulled-back Hasse vanishing order. Then g_P=0 at ordinary P and Σ_{P∈C(k)}g_P(m)=|q_L(m)|(ω.C), with finite support. A subset sum such as over C∩Z(m) is only ≤ the total, unless it contains all positive-Hasse-order points.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 7.6, from Maulik–Shankar–Tang Definition 7.1.3
items.note: g_P(m) is the share of the global intersection number that the point P would contribute if there were no decay; the theorem is proved by showing the true local contribution is a constant fraction α' < 1 of it.

items.name: The global bound on local intersection multiplicities
items.statement: There is a constant c_1 depending only on C with i_P(C.Z(m)) ≤ (C.Z(m)) < c_1 m^{b/2} for every P and every m.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, equation (7.2) in §7.7, from Lemma 7.5
items.note: This is the only place the algebraicity of C is used, and by §3.5 it cannot be dispensed with: for a formal curve the local multiplicities can grow exponentially.

items.name: Successive minima of the lattices L_n
items.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ r = rk_Z L_n, the i-th successive minimum μ_i(n) of L_n is inf{y > 0 : there are linearly independent v_1,…,v_i ∈ L_n with Q(v_j) ≤ y^2}; set a_i(n) = ∏_{j≤i}μ_j(n) and a_0(n) = 1.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Definition 7.8, in the normalisation of Eskin
items.note: Keeping the individual successive minima, and not only the determinant, is what makes the lattice-point bounds uniform across the infinite family {L_n}. GN.1 plans successive minima; the reviewed audit finds them unbuilt, not unplanned.

items.name: Uniform lattice-point counts in terms of the successive minima
items.statement: For a positive definite quadratic lattice of rank r with successive minima μ_i and a_i = ∏_{j≤i}μ_j, the number of lattice points v with Q(v) ≤ Y is at most an absolute constant depending only on r times Σ_{i=0}^r Y^{i/2}/a_i.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, used in the proofs of Propositions 7.11 and 7.13, quoted from Eskin, Lemma 2.4 and equations (5) and (6)
items.note: The point of this form of the estimate is that the implied constant depends only on the rank, so it may be applied to every member of the nested family at once.

items.name: A lower bound for the successive minima along the family (Lemma 7.9)
items.statement: a_i(n) ≫ n^{i/b} for 1 ≤ i ≤ rk_Z L_n, with the implied constant depending only on C.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 7.9
items.note: Proved by taking a minimal vector v ∈ L_n, noting v ∈ L_i for i ≤ n, and comparing i_P(C.Z(Q(v))) ≥ n with the global bound; then μ_i(n) ≥ μ_1(n) gives the higher minima.

items.name: Truncation of the lattice-count sum (Corollary 7.10)
items.statement: There is a constant c_2 depending only on C with Σ_{m ∈ S_X} i_P(C.Z(m)) = Σ_{n=1}^{c_2 X^{b/2}} Σ_{m ∈ S_X} #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Corollary 7.10
items.note: For n beyond c_2X^{b/2} the shortest vector of L_n already has Q(v) > 2X, so those levels contribute nothing; this is what makes all later sums finite.

items.name: The local contribution at a non-supersingular point is negligible (Proposition 7.11)
items.statement: For P not supersingular, Σ_{m=1}^{2X} i_P(C.Z(m)) = O(X^{b/2}log X), with the implied constant depending only on C; in particular the same bound holds for Σ_{m ∈ S_X} i_P(C.Z(m)).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 7.11
items.note: Uses rk_Z L_n ≤ b at such a point, together with Lemma 7.9 and the uniform lattice count; the logarithm appears only in the boundary case i = b.

items.name: The splitting of the supersingular local contribution into a main term and an error
items.statement: For a supersingular P and a parameter T, write Σ_{m ∈ S_X} i_P(C.Z(m)) = i_P(X,T)_err + i_P(X,T)_mt where the error term sums the levels T ≤ n ≤ c_2X^{b/2} and the main term the levels n < T.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.12
items.note: T is chosen at the very end of the proof of Theorem 7.18, depending only on α, α' and S; the decay lemmas are what make the main term small, and Lemma 7.9 what makes the error term small.

items.name: The error term is uniformly small (Proposition 7.13)
items.statement: There is an absolute constant c_3 > 0, independent of X and T, with i_P(X,T)_err ≤ (c_3/T^{2/b})X^{(b+2)/2} + O(X^{(b+1)/2}).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 7.13, whose proof contains a misprint in the exponent of T (see sourceIssues)
items.note: Only the case i = b+2 of the lattice count survives at the top of the range, and there the tail of Σ n^{-(b+2)/b} is of size T^{-2/b}.

items.name: Theta series of the auxiliary lattices L'_n and their Eisenstein parts
items.statement: Choose L_n ⊂ L'_n ⊂ L_n ⊗ Q with L'_n maximal at every ℓ ≠ p, L'_n ⊗ Z_p = L_n ⊗ Z_p and L'_n ⊂ L'_1. Let θ_n be the theta series of L'_n, with coefficients r_n(m) ≥ #{v ∈ L_n : Q(v) = m}; θ_n is a modular form of weight 1+b/2 and splits as an Eisenstein series E_{L'_n} plus a cusp form. Writing q_{L'_n}(m) for the Eisenstein coefficients and g(m) for those of Σ_{n≤T}G_n, the trivial bound gives g(m) = O_T(m^{(b+2)/4}), whence i_P(X,T)_mt ≤ Σ_{n≤T}Σ_{m ∈ S_X} q_{L'_n}(m) + O_T(X^{1+(b+2)/4}).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §7.14
items.note: Enlarging L_n away from p is what makes the theta series a modular form for a manageable level while leaving the p-adic data, which is all the decay lemmas control, untouched.

items.name: The Siegel mass formula for the auxiliary lattices (Theorem 7.15)
items.statement: Let L'_1 be the positive definite auxiliary rank b+2 lattice, maximal away from p, and L'⊂L'_1 with identical Z_ℓ-localizations for ℓ≠p. Put d'=|L'^∨/L'|, Δ_1=det L'_1, and C_b(m) as item70. For even b, χ'=χ_{(−1)^{1+b/2}4Δ_1} and q_{L'}(m)=C_b(m)σ_{−b/2}(m,χ')/[√d' L(1+b/2,χ')]·∏_{ℓ|2Δ_1}δ(ℓ,L',m). For odd b, m=m_0f² with (f,2Δ_1)=1 and v_ℓ(m_0)∈{0,1} outside 2Δ_1, D'=(−1)^{(b−1)/2}2m_0Δ_1, and q_{L'}(m)=C_b(m)L((b+1)/2,χ_{D'})/[√d' ζ(b+1)]·[Σ_{a|f}μ(a)χ_{D'}(a)a^{−(b+1)/2}σ_{−b}(f/a)]·∏_{ℓ|2Δ_1}[δ(ℓ,L',m)/(1−ℓ^{−1−b})]. Use D' in BOTH L-value and divisor sum. Match the positive sign, Gram determinants and primitive/imprimitive conventions.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 7.15, with the corrected character in the odd case (see sourceIssues)
items.note: The formulae are exactly parallel to Theorem 7.4 with L replaced by L'; comparing the two, term by term, is what gives Lemma 7.16. The review rejected inherited E4 as a demonstrated error: χ_D and χ_{D'} agree on the allowed divisors of f. The uniform D' presentation here makes that comparison explicit.

items.name: The Eisenstein coefficients decay with the discriminant (Lemma 7.16)
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 7.16
items.note: The proof bounds the local density at p by 2 in general, and by 1+p^{-1} in the superspecial case by an induction on the rank of the reduced lattice; this refinement at superspecial points is what the sharper decay of Theorem 3.3 is paired with.

items.name: The supersingular main term is a fixed fraction of the expected share (Proposition 7.17)
items.statement: Under the standing proper generically ordinary curve hypotheses, for supersingular P there exists 0<α<1 independent of X,T with i_P(X,T)_mt ≤ αΣ_{m∈S_X}g_P(m)+O_T(X^{1+(b+2)/4}). This is an upper bound, not an asymptotic equality.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 7.17, whose proof contains an arithmetic misprint in the non-superspecial case (see sourceIssues)
items.note: Majorants are 11/12 (non-superspecial), 61/62 (b≥4 superspecial first alternative), 17/20 (second alternative). The b=3 first branch imports a rank-three theorem from earlier MST. The constants bound the series; no attained local ratio is claimed.

items.name: The total supersingular contribution (Theorem 7.18)
items.statement: A fixed 0<α'<1 bounds Σ_{m∈S_X}i_P(C.Z(m)) ≤ α'Σ_{m∈S_X}g_P(m)+O(X^{(b+1)/2}) at supersingular P. Choose fixed T to absorb c_3T^{−2/b}X^{1+b/2} into (α'−α)Σg_P. Combine this upper bound, the nonsupersingular estimate and the all-point Hasse-degree inequality for the finite-support contradiction.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Theorem 7.18
items.note: Replace the printed equalities by ≤ also in the last step of the proof of Theorem1.2. This repair does not close the other local proof gates.

items.name: Integral models of the minimal and toroidal compactifications of a Hodge-type Shimura variety
items.statement: For a canonical integral model 𝒮 of a Hodge-type Shimura variety with hyperspecial level at p, Madapusi Pera constructs a projective normal compactification 𝒮^BB over Z_(p) whose generic fibre is the Baily–Borel compactification, with a flat stratification by quotients of integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type, and, for an admissible complete smooth cone decomposition, a smooth toroidal compactification 𝒮^tor whose generic fibre is the toroidal compactification of Ash–Mumford–Rapoport–Tai and Pink, stratified by mixed Shimura varieties with flat boundary divisors, together with π: 𝒮^tor → 𝒮^BB extending the identity and compatible with the stratifications. Prime-to-p Hecke correspondences extend to the minimal compactification. Toroidal extensions require compatible source/target fans and common-refinement comparisons, not all correspondences on one arbitrary fan; the canonical one-dimensional cusp case is item89.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.1, quoting Madapusi Pera, Theorems 1, 2, 3 and 4.1.5
items.note: Everything in §8 is carried out in these integral compactifications; in particular the Hecke correspondences on them are algebraic, which is what makes the Zariski closures Hecke-stable.

items.name: Coordinates at a 0-dimensional cusp and the action of 𝔹_ℓ
items.statement: For a 0-dimensional cusp with cusp label Φ and admissible parabolic P, let U_P be its unipotent radical and W the centre of U_P; to the level K_n one attaches the lattice 𝐁_{K_n} ⊂ W(Q) with dual 𝐒_{K_n}, an arithmetic group Δ_{K_n} acting on it, and an open self-adjoint cone 𝐇 ⊂ W(R). The complete local ring of 𝒮^BB_{n,k} at the cusp is R_{ℓ^n} = k[[q^λ]]_{λ ≥ 0}^{Δ_{K_n}}, and R_ℓ = ∪_n R_{ℓ^n}. The group 𝔹_ℓ = 𝐁_{K_n} ⊗ Z[1/ℓ] fixes the point of the inverse limit and acts on R_ℓ by Σ a_λ q^λ ↦ Σ 𝐞((T,λ))a_λ q^λ, where 𝐞: Z[1/ℓ] → μ_{ℓ^∞}(k) is determined by the cusp and the level structure.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.2, following Madapusi Pera §§2.1.11–2.1.18 and Corollaries 5.1.8 and 5.2.8
items.note: These are exactly the coordinates in which Chai's cancellation argument for 𝒜_g is carried out, and the reason it transfers verbatim.

items.name: Invariant ideals at a 0-dimensional cusp lie in the boundary (Proposition 8.3)
items.statement: Let I_{ℓ^n} ⊂ R_{ℓ^n} be a non-zero ideal such that I = I_{ℓ^n}R is stable under 𝔹_ℓ. Then Spf R_{ℓ^n}/I_{ℓ^n} is contained in the formal completion of the boundary of 𝒮^BB_{n,k}.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 8.3, after Chai, Proposition 2
items.note: Proved by passing to a toroidal chart and producing, for each cone σ, an element of I with a leading term with respect to the toroidal boundary ideal; the key step is Chai's purely cone-theoretic cancellation algorithm, which applies unchanged.

items.name: The Hecke action near a 1-dimensional cusp
items.statement: For a 1-dimensional cusp the cone decomposition is unique and the corresponding boundary strata of 𝒮^tor are canonical, so the prime-to-p Hecke action extends uniquely to π^{-1}(𝒮^BB minus the 0-dimensional cusps); consequently the intersection of the Zariski closure of a Hecke orbit with that open set is Hecke-stable.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, §8.4, from Madapusi Pera Proposition 2.1.19, §4.1.12 and Proposition 4.1.13, and Bruinier–Zemel §3.3
items.note: Canonicity of the boundary strata over 1-dimensional cusps is what makes the Hecke action available there at all; over a 0-dimensional cusp it is not, which is why that case is treated separately.

items.name: Hecke translates at a 1-dimensional cusp in characteristic zero (Proposition 8.6)
items.statement: For y ∈ π^{-1}(Υ(C)) and T_{y,ℓ} the set of ℓ-power Hecke translates of y, T_{y,ℓ} contains all the translates of y by ℓ-power torsion points of ℰ_{π(y)} ⊗ Λ, where π^{-1}(π(y)) is an ℰ_{π(y)} ⊗ Λ-torsor.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 8.6
items.note: The proof identifies the action of 𝒱(Q) = (U/W)(Q) on the torsor explicitly and uses that U is a Heisenberg group, so every element of 𝒱(Z[1/ℓ]) lifts to U(Z[1/ℓ]).

items.name: Density of Hecke translates in a fibre over a 1-dimensional cusp (Corollary 8.7)
items.statement: For y ∈ π^{-1}(Υ(k)) with Υ a 1-dimensional cusp of 𝒮^BB, the set T_{y,ℓ} ∩ π^{-1}(π(y)) is Zariski dense in π^{-1}(π(y)).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Corollary 8.7
items.note: The characteristic-p statement follows from Proposition 8.6 because the boundary strata over 1-dimensional cusps are canonical and the Hecke action there is the reduction of the one in characteristic zero.

items.name: The 1-dimensional-cusp dichotomy (Corollary 8.8)
items.statement: Let x ∈ 𝒮_{F_p}(k) be ordinary with b ≥ 3. If the closure of the Hecke orbit in 𝒮^BB_k contains a k-point on a 1-dimensional cusp, then either the closure of the Hecke orbit is all of 𝒮_k, or its boundary is 0-dimensional and the closure in 𝒮^BB_k has dimension at least 2.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Corollary 8.8
items.note: Case (2) is what makes the second alternative usable: a projective variety of dimension at least 2 contains a proper curve avoiding any finite set of points.

items.name: Existence of a generically ordinary proper curve in the Hecke closure (Proposition 8.9)
items.statement: For an ordinary x ∈ 𝒮_{F_p}(k), either the Zariski closure of its prime-to-p Hecke orbit is all of 𝒮_k, or it contains a proper curve that is generically ordinary.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Proposition 8.9 of the accepted version; this statement is not in arXiv:2011.08887v1
items.note: The proof separates the case b = 2, where 1-dimensional cusps exist exactly when 𝒮 is a product of two modular curves, from the case where 𝒮^BB has no 1-dimensional cusps, and otherwise appeals to Corollary 8.8.

items.name: Hecke stability and ℓ-adic monodromy (Lemma 8.10)
items.statement: A morphism of Hodge-type data at compatible hyperspecial levels induces f:𝒮_1→𝒮_2. For nonempty X⊂𝒮_{2,k} meeting the ordinary locus, the prime-to-p orbit closure T̄_X pulls back to a Hecke-stable f^{-1}(T̄_X). For noncontainment use a PROPER Shimura subvariety Z whose group image in G_2^ad is proper: dense adjoint monodromy then precludes T̄_X⊂Z_k. The full arithmetic-monodromy proof is an obligation; the word subvariety cannot replace these hypotheses.
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 8.10 of the accepted version, which is Lemma 8.9 of arXiv:2011.08887v1
items.note: Clause (1) is proved by showing the ℓ-adic monodromy of the universal abelian variety over a Hecke-stable subvariety is Zariski dense in G_2^ad over Q_ℓ; the accepted version spells this argument out in full, using that the Frobenius at an ordinary point has non-identity component in each Q-simple factor.

items.name: The proper curve may be chosen outside every special divisor (Lemma 8.11)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 8.9 the proper curve in the closure of the Hecke orbit may be chosen not to lie in any special divisor Z(m).
items.locator: Maulik–Shankar–Tang, accepted version of 25 December 2021, Lemma 8.11 of the accepted version; this statement is not in arXiv:2011.08887v1
items.note: Proved from Lemma 8.10 (1) by choosing a curve with the same ℓ-adic monodromy as an irreducible component of the closure whose monodromy is Zariski dense in G^ad. Descend the finite data to F_q and apply Hilbert irreducibility over the global field F_q(t), not F̄_p(t). Distinguish arithmetic and geometric monodromy and prove compatibility with a proper curve avoiding the finite boundary; these interfaces remain gates.

items.name: The unitary case (Remark 8.12)
items.statement: Let p≥5 split in the imaginary quadratic K, and let the signature(n,1) Hermitian lattice be self-dual at p. For a smooth irreducible proper generically ordinary curve mapping finitely to the hyperspecial PEL model and contained in no special divisor, the unitary analogue gives infinitely many points on special divisors of prime-to-p norm, via the orthogonal reduction and required low-dimensional base cases. Ordinary prime-to-p Hecke orbits are dense. The minimal boundary has dimension zero; the canonical toroidal fibres are the stated CM-elliptic torsors E⊗_{O_K}Λ_0 up to finite quotient, rank Λ_0=n−1. Retain the polarization, level and moduli hypotheses of Remark8.12.

items.note: This is the second half of Theorem 1.4. Only the 0-dimensional cusp analysis is needed, because the unitary Baily–Borel boundary has no 1-dimensional components.

prerequisites.citation: Arthur Ogus, "Supersingular K3 crystals", Journées de Géométrie Algébrique de Rennes (1978), Astérisque 64 (1979), 3–86

prerequisites.citation: Arthur Ogus, "Singularities of the height strata in the moduli of K3 surfaces", in Moduli of abelian varieties (Texel Island, 1999), Progr. Math. 195, Birkhäuser (2001), 325–343
prerequisites.why: The local equations of the Newton, that is height, strata in the formal neighbourhood of a supersingular point (Lemma 2, Proposition 11), and the fact that the non-ordinary locus is singular exactly at the superspecial points (proof of Corollary 16). These are what Corollary 4.10 and Theorem 5.15 rest on.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Kisin, "Integral models for Shimura varieties of abelian type", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 23 (2010), 967–1012
prerequisites.why: The canonical smooth integral model 𝒮 at hyperspecial level (Theorem 2.3.8), the transitivity of the Hecke action on connected components (Lemma 2.2.5), and, above all, the description of the formal neighbourhood of a point of the special fibre as the completion of the opposite unipotent, with the Frobenius on the crystal given by u ∘ (φ ⊗ σ) (§§1.4–1.5, and the construction of the horizontal section in §1.5.5). §4.8 and the whole of §5 are built on that description.

prerequisites.why: The Kuga–Satake abelian scheme over the integral model, the local systems 𝐋_? inside End_{C(L)}(𝐇_?) with their compatibilities (Propositions 3.11, 3.12, 4.7), the quadratic form with v ∘ v = [Q(v)] (Lemma 5.2), and the criterion that speciality may be checked crystallinely in the special fibre (Corollary 5.22, §5.24).

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: crystalline decay and ordinary Hecke orbits
routes.brief: Extend ShimuraVarieties in characteristic p; do not create an unrelated direction merely because a K3 application accompanies a Hecke-orbit theorem. For p≥5 and the self-dual orthogonal integral model of signature (b,2), the primary final target is Theorem1.2: every smooth proper irreducible generically ordinary curve mapping finitely to the model and contained in no Z(m) meets ∪_{p∤m}Z(m) in infinitely many geometric points. Theorem1.4 then asserts density of prime-to-p ordinary Hecke orbits, including the split-at-p unitary signature-(n,1) case with prime-to-p discriminant and its low-dimensional base cases. Theorem1.1 is the K3 application, for a non-isotrivial generically ordinary family over a proper curve whose generic Picard discriminant is prime to p; import the period-map/K3 comparison from a common K3 owner instead of building it twice. Conjecture1.3 is only a proposition to state. Cover the Ogus supersingular lattice/type/cyclic-vector classification, Kisin coordinate display and weight-zero Frobenius, t-adically convergent horizontal product, minimal-tuple combinatorics and the de Jong obstruction imported from route7. Separate Teichmüller lift valuations from mod-p valuations: source issues E14–E16 currently block the superspecial proof. The generalized Newton-stratum Theorem5.15 is an unproved extension target under E13, not a supplier. Build the index/minima bounds, positive-density represented set, uniform lattice counts and theta-series comparison using GN.1/GN.3/GN.4 and route2. Use upper bounds, not asymptotic equalities, in the supersingular main-term comparison; sum Hasse orders over all of C for the divisor-degree equality. Import route3's integral boundary charts, then prove Chai cancellation, one-cusp orbit propagation, proper-curve selection with finite-field Hilbert irreducibility/monodromy, and induction. Import R07.2/R07.6, CR.0/CR.1/CR.3, A4, pinned Witt/Clifford/covolume/L-functions and fine modular curves. Preserve all hypotheses and allocate generic finite-field Hilbert/monodromy and the historical Green–Oguiso comparison to their common owners before design. None of these proof gaps is filled by naming an import.

The printed χ_D in the mass formula is not a confirmed mistake: χ_D and χ_D′ agree on its divisor support (rejected E4). This coalesces with the number-field companion's same source route.

Reuse TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantCharFun and DirichletCharacter.twistedDivisorSum for their actual scopes. The residual source adapter constructs the full discriminant character including imprimitive moduli and proves the coefficient comparison for σ_s(m,χ) with negative/real s, which the existing natural-exponent two-character sum does not directly provide. This is an AN.1 coefficient/L-value interface; generic finite-sum algebra is not a new analytic-number-theory roadmap.

Import the completed PD envelope from CR.0 (item97), prove the coefficientwise nonintegrality test used in §5.6, and identify the special-tensor horizontal continuation under crystalline realization. The de Jong §2.3 theorem and compatibility hypotheses have not been independently extracted here; this route is reserved but rejected pending that work. sourceIssues.correction: the middle expression is 2(p² + p − 1)/(p(p² − 1)); the two summands of the numerator are transposed
sourceIssues.reason: The displayed series is (2/(1-p^{-2}))(h(p^{-1}+1)/p² + hp/p⁴ + hp²/p⁶ + ···). Summing the geometric tail, the bracket is h((p+1)/p³ + 1/(p²(p-1))) = h(p²+p-1)/(p³(p-1)), and multiplying by 2p²/(p²-1) gives exactly (h/(p-1))·2(p²+p-1)/(p(p²-1)). At p = 3 this is 22/24 = 11/12, which is where the constant 11/12 comes from and shows the bound is sharp there; numerically, with h = 1 and p = 3 the series is (9/4)(4/27 + 1/18) = 0.4583… = (11/12)·(1/2), confirming it. The printed 2(p²-p+1)/(p(p²-1)) equals 7/12 at p = 3, so as printed the first inequality of the chain is false, although the final bound 11/12 that the proof uses is correct. The same computation carried out for the two superspecial cases of the same proof reproduces the printed constants exactly, 61/62 at p = 5 in case (1) and 17/20 at p = 5 in case (2), which confirms the method.
